Second-order terms of the dispersion and of the centroid gap

Source: R/algebra-dispersion.R
local_terms.Rd

Compares the dispersion \(H\) and the gap between the mean reliability and the informativeness with their second-order approximations, and bounds the remainders.

Usage

local_terms(S)

Arguments

S

Site reliabilities, a numeric vector of numbers strictly between 0 and 1, as returned by site_reliability().

Value

A data frame with two rows, H and gap (the mean reliability minus \(I\)), and the columns

  • quantity: "H" or "gap".

  • exact: the value of the quantity.

  • leading: its second-order term.

  • bound: the bound on the absolute remainder.

  • holds: TRUE if the absolute leading term is larger than the bound, NA if both are 0, as when all the reliabilities are equal.

Details

Proposition 2 of Lee (2026) gives, with the logit variance \(V\) and the third absolute logit moment \(\rho_3\) of logit_moments(), $$H = \tfrac12 I(1-I)V + R_H, \qquad |R_H| \le \frac{\sqrt3}{108}\rho_3,$$ $$\bar S - I = \tfrac12 I(1-I)(1-2I)V + R_S, \qquad |R_S| \le \frac{\rho_3}{48}.$$ When the leading term is larger than the bound in absolute value, the exact value has the sign of the leading term. For the gap, that sign is the sign of \(1 - 2I\), so the mean reliability is above \(I\) when \(I < 1/2\). When the bound is the larger, the remainder can decide the sign, and the gap can have the other sign; the exact column always gives the value itself.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

S <- site_reliability(se = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30), sigma_tau = 0.2)
local_terms(S)
#>   quantity        exact     leading      bound holds
#> 1        H  0.075692420  0.07896183 0.01082354  TRUE
#> 2      gap -0.009505495 -0.01128026 0.01406019 FALSE

# A skewed profile of 25 sites with I = 0.3 and V = 2 whose mean
# reliability is below I, against the sign of the leading term.
d <- c(sqrt(48), rep(-sqrt(1 / 12), 24))
local_terms(plogis(qlogis(0.3) + d))
#>   quantity       exact leading     bound holds
#> 1        H  0.15398567   0.210 0.2137037 FALSE
#> 2      gap -0.02675316   0.084 0.2776093 FALSE
